provenance.notes: Operator-confirmed outcomes: start, stop. 2026-07-09: data_type relabelled BOOL -> INT8 when DataType was remapped to the official spec coding; the captured wire byte (0x01) is unchanged.

provenance.method: active send (tools/control/send_settings_command.py --packet video_format --dimension-enum sweep, 2026-07-21). Coordinates now confirmed working, not just a hypothesis: repeated real-hardware sends produced genuine, repeatable resolution transitions on the recording_format (0x01/0x09) mode-notify channel — operator-confirmed against the on-screen resolution name after a power cycle (see notes). video_format's own channel (0x01/0x00) still never echoes, matching POCKET_6K_G2_v7.9. Not yet promoted to VERIFIED — that requires the full CameraSession round trip (examples/change_codec.py), not yet attempted on this camera.
provenance.notes: IMPORTANT, real-hardware confirmed 2026-07-21: this camera's on-screen settings display does NOT live-update after a video_format write — the change genuinely takes effect (confirmed both by the wire and by power-cycling the camera, which then shows the new value) — but the body's menu keeps showing the OLD value until rebooted. Do not treat a static on-screen display alone as evidence a write failed; check tools/captures/ or power-cycle to confirm. dimension_enum values found so far match POCKET_6K_G2_v7.9's numbers exactly for every resolution tested (independently confirmed on this camera's own captures, not copied — see the resolutions table below) — 0x02 also produced a transition to the same pixel dimensions as 0x13 ('6K') once, but with fps clamped to 30 instead of the requested 50 and no confirming echo on a repeat attempt; recorded as an open, unresolved candidate rather than a second dimension_enums entry (the schema only holds one enum per resolution/codec pair) — see the '6K' resolution entry's own comment.

4K DCI._comment: Camera offers 4K DCI under both codecs (operator-confirmed), but the only known dimension_enum (8) reaches BRAW's 4K DCI only — same unresolved gap as POCKET_6K_G2_v7.9's 4K DCI/ProRes (docs/settings.md §7-§9), independently observed here, not assumed from the G2.

6K._comment: dimension_enum 19 (0x13) cleanly reproduced this resolution at the requested 50fps. Enum 2 (0x02) also produced the same pixel dimensions once, but clamped fps to 30 and did not reproduce on a later attempt (no confirming echo that time) — left unresolved rather than recorded as a second candidate, since the schema holds only one enum per resolution/codec pair. frame_flags reported as 0x00 here vs 0x10 for every other resolution — matches the G2's 'windowed bit' hypothesis (0x00 = full sensor, 0x10 = windowed/cropped), consistent with a full-sensor readout mode plausibly explaining the lower fps ceiling.

50._comment: CANDIDATE (fps_modes has no per-entry provenance field in the schema). fps_int directly observed on the wire (passive recording_format 0x01/0x09 reports, tools/captures/POCKET_6K_PRO_v8.6/POCKET_6K_PRO_v8.6_20260721T171924.json). frame_flags is genuinely resolution-dependent at this fps on real captures (0x00 for HD/UHD, 0x10 for 4K DCI — same 'windowed bit' pattern already flagged for the G2, docs/settings.md) but this table only holds one value per fps; 0 chosen as the 2-of-3-resolutions default — revisit if a recording_format write at 4K DCI needs the 0x10 variant. m_rate=0 is an untested candidate (video_format has never been sent yet) — reasonable for a round, non-NTSC rate but not confirmed.

provenance.method: passive observation from examples/record_start_stop.py real-hardware logs during induced SD card slow-write-speed testing
provenance.notes: Raw bytes FF 07 00 00 09 01 01 02 00 FE 00. Payload byte at offset 1 flips 0x01 (nominal) -> 0xFE (-2, low_margin) 0.1-1.4s before every autonomous unexpected stop observed on a known-slow SD card — 6/6 occurrences, 3 cycles x 2 camera models (POCKET_6K_G2 v7.9, POCKET_6K_PRO v8.6). Never -2 in 7 unrelated normal-session logs, where this notification fires once per session and stays 0x01. Payload offsets 0 and 2 are constant (0x00) in every sample, both conditions. NOT yet isolated from other possible autostop causes (card full, card removed, power loss) — 'slow write speed' is inference from test context, not read off the wire alone. See docs/recording.md's 'Camera-initiated stop detection' section.
